items.exemplar: (a) The patent system let inventors claim legal ownership of their ideas, which encouraged invention by promising inventors a chance to profit from their work. (b) The telephone let managers coordinate distant offices, factories, and markets instantly, which made it practical to run large corporations across a national market. (c) Both tied the national market together, but differently: railroads moved goods and people cheaply over long distances, while the telephone moved information instantly, letting businesses manage far-flung operations.
